name: Oscillator-as-delay: LFO repeats + stepped pitch-shift grains
goal: Emulate granular pitching delays inside the synth (no delay FX): second oscillator copies the dry WT, an envelope-shaped tempo-synced LFO repeats its level like echoes, global amp release sets feedback/fade length, a fade-in LFO avoids overlapping the dry attack, and a stepped envelope-mode LFO raises pitch by octaves each repeat (e.g. +24 st over quarter-note steps) for sanding granular delay tails—then share formant/WT macros with the dry osc.

source.title: How to Turn Any Synth Into a Granular Delay ✨ | Vital Pad Tutorial

prerequisites: Multi-osc wavetable synth with per-osc level modulation, multiple LFOs (tempo sync + envelope mode), filter, macros

inputs.name: delay_subdivision
inputs.description: e.g. quarter or eighth note LFO rate for repeats

inputs.name: pitch_step_semitones
inputs.description: Total pitch rise across steps (transcript example +24)

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Delta vs ping-pong-delay / granular-dual-saw: delay is synthesized by a second oscillator + LFO envelopes, not an FX delay or granular engine plugin.

steps.action: Dry voice: osc1 on basic/WT shape; use a non-global envelope (env2) on osc1 level so amp envelope 1’s release can later control delay ring-out. Filter with driven LP (~24 dB), key track, env3→cutoff (decay/release up, sustain ~halfway, some attack).
steps.expect: Expressive dry tone with independent delay headroom

steps.action: Optional: sculpt WT (sine↔saw spectral blend), macro→WT position + cutoff; velocity→filter attack and env3 depth for soft vs bright hits; light unison (~2%).
Delay osc: enable osc2, copy osc1 waveform. Instead of an ADSR on level, draw an echo-like shape on LFO1 and map it to osc2 level; tempo-sync LFO1 to set delay time.
steps.expect: Repeating amplitude taps like a delay

steps.action: Feedback/fade: use global envelope release to control how long repeats die out. Fade-in: another LFO in envelope mode with a ramp-up modulating the delay-level mod depth so repeats don’t pile on the dry attack.
steps.expect: Delays appear after the dry transient

steps.action: Granular pitch sanding: LFO in envelope/step mode → osc2 pitch; set amount to +24 semitones (two octaves) with steps aligned to the delay subdivision (e.g. each quarter step up) so each repeat rises in pitch like a granular pitch-shift delay.

Link formant-scale / WT position macros so delay osc timbre tracks the dry sound. Optional reverse-delay style LFOs: leave space in the shape to fade down and avoid clicks; try faster eighth-note rates.

verification: Mute osc2 → only dry; solo osc2 → pitched repeating taps
Longer amp release lengthens delay tail
Pitch-step LFO raises each repeat (e.g. toward +2 octaves)
